issues.message: Thin PEC thin_conductor[0] ('thin_conductor[0]', realized as a sheet) has a metal plane at z = 800µm (node 18) with asymmetric neighbouring cells (400µm below, 100µm above, ratio 4.00). Meep/OpenEMS require equal cell sizes across a metal plane; radiation pattern may be corrupted (issue #48). Put the metal plane on a preserved-region boundary or refine the neighbouring cell.

Thin PEC thin_conductor[1] ('thin_conductor[1]', realized as a sheet) has a metal plane at z = 1.9mm (node 21) with asymmetric neighbouring cells (500µm below, 100µm above, ratio 5.00). Meep/OpenEMS require equal cell sizes across a metal plane; radiation pattern may be corrupted (issue #48). Put the metal plane on a preserved-region boundary or refine the neighbouring cell.
No sources, ports, TFSF, or waveguide/Floquet/MSL ports configured. Simulation will produce zero fields.

dz_profile max adjacent cell ratio 5.000 exceeds the validated multi-band grading cap 1.4 (docs/guides/support_matrix.md, 'Multi-band graded mesh'). WHY: stability is unaffected (dt is the global min-cell CFL, sufficient on any tensor grid), but per-transition accuracy is witnessed only along z and only up to ratio 1.4 — the -54 dB reflection class at 30 cells/wavelength (it scales as (dz/lambda)^2), against -44 dB measured at ratio 2.0. COST: an unquantified reflection and grading-dispersion error at that transition. REMEDY: split it into ratio<=1.4 steps (e.g. rfx.smooth_grading) to stay inside the validated envelope, or accept it and say so in the report. STALE-IF: the support-matrix row raises the cap.

Box material 'core' rasterizes to 2 z cells (implied 10.0) over z-span [900µm, 1.9mm). smooth_grading transition cells may have shifted the fine band — derive z coordinates from the actual fine-band edges and assert the rasterized cell count (issue #325)

all dielectric(s) ['core'] are perfectly lossless in an open (CPML) domain. If you are measuring Q / resonance, this gives an ARTIFICIALLY infinite Q (design-guide Anti-Pattern #1, an R5 surface-metric trap) — add loss, e.g. sigma = 2*pi*f*eps0*eps_r*tan_delta. (Harmless if you are not measuring Q.)

2 PEC sheet(s) realized (lattice ownership contract #931 §1.3: one node plane each, closed footprint, normal E through the plane live), 2 of them off their declared mid-plane; worst first: thin_conductor[0] 'thin_conductor[0]' normal z: declared mid-plane 850µm, realized node plane 18 at 800µm (offset -0.500 cell = 50µm); thin_conductor[1] 'thin_conductor[1]' normal z: declared mid-plane 1.95mm, realized node plane 21 at 1.9mm (offset -0.500 cell = 50µm). A sheet snaps to the node plane nearest its declared mid-plane (an exact half-cell tie resolves LOWER); an offset means the declared plane — a laminate face, a ground level — is not on this mesh's node line, and the conductor sits that far from where it was drawn. REMEDY when the offset matters: put a mesh node on the declared plane (dx = h/N for an interface at height h, or a preserved region on the non-uniform lane). COVERAGE: every sheet declaration on the nonuniform lane (zero-thickness PEC Boxes via add() and PEC add_thin_conductor entries). STALE IF: the named sheet's SheetSpec.plane is not the printed node.

2 PEC sheet(s) declared with a mid-plane on an exact half-cell TIE between two node planes: thin_conductor[0] 'thin_conductor[0]' normal z: declared mid-plane 850µm is equidistant from node planes 18 (800µm) and 19 (900µm); realized on the LOWER one, plane 18; thin_conductor[1] 'thin_conductor[1]' normal z: declared mid-plane 1.95mm is equidistant from node planes 21 (1.9mm) and 22 (2mm); realized on the LOWER one, plane 21. A face-registered one-cell foil (both faces on nodes, mid-plane at the cell centre) is this case; the contract resolves the tie to the lower plane so existing declarations land where they always did, but the choice is a rule, not the drawing. REMEDY: declare the sheet ON the plane you mean (a zero-thickness Box at that coordinate) so no tie is resolved for you.

4 conductor sheet dimension(s) are solved more than 1% off their drawn size (worst 4 listed): thin_conductor[0] 'thin_conductor[0]' x: drawn 6mm, nodes cover 6mm, solved as 6.35mm (+5.83%); thin_conductor[0] 'thin_conductor[0]' y: drawn 6mm, nodes cover 6mm, solved as 6.35mm (+5.83%); thin_conductor[1] 'thin_conductor[1]' x: drawn 6mm, nodes cover 6mm, solved as 6.35mm (+5.83%); thin_conductor[1] 'thin_conductor[1]' y: drawn 6mm, nodes cover 6mm, solved as 6.35mm (+5.83%). OBSERVED: the node span the sheet's realized footprint covers on this run's grid, plus 0.35 of the adjacent cell at each free in-plane edge -- a PEC sheet's edge is solved that far beyond its last node (measured on this solver, both polarizations; a flat wall has no such offset). REMEDY: build the in-plane profiles with rfx.mesh_edges.edge_aware_profiles(domain, dx, sheets=[...], solids=[...]) and pass them as Simulation(dx_profile=..., dy_profile=...); a node ON the edge is not the fix. STALE IF: the footprint's node span on the run's node coordinates does not reproduce the printed numbers.

1 conductor-bounded cavit(y/ies) differ from the physical stack by more than 1% in electrical thickness: [z] thin_conductor[0] (sheet, plane k=18 at 800µm, declared face 900µm, snap -100µm)/thin_conductor[1] (sheet, k=21 at 1.9mm, declared face 1.9mm, snap +1.518e-09nm) at in-plane column (26,26): sum(d/eps) mesh 350µm vs physical 250µm (+40.0%); sum(d*sqrt(eps)) mesh 2.1mm vs physical 2mm (+5.0%); plane-to-plane 1.1mm vs face-to-face 1mm; the capacitance measure (sum d/eps) governs (gap << lambda at freq_max). OBSERVED: mesh sums run over the cells strictly between two adjacent REALIZED wall planes (rfx.boundaries.pec.realized_wall_planes on each conductor's own edges) on the run's own spacings and assembled eps_r; physical sums run between the DECLARED faces through the geometry Box spans at the pair's shared column. The difference is exactly the printed per-plane snap (a declared face that is not on a node realizes on the nearest node plane; a sheet realizes on one plane, so a foil declared with two faces reads its thickness as cavity — the sheet model's honest cost) plus any vacuum cell the drawing left at a sheet plane. WHY BOTH MEASURES: the same defect class measured 17.3% as a series capacitance and 3.2% as phase length (#703) — a bare percentage invites 'correcting' a right number into a wrong one, so both are printed and the governing one is named. REMEDY: put the declared faces on mesh nodes (dx = h/N, or preserved regions on the non-uniform lane) and, for a foil, declare the sheet ON the interface it bounds so no snap is resolved for you; a vacuum cell is fixed by extending the dielectric to the sheet plane. Nothing else is a defect: a plane-to-plane cavity that equals the declared stack is what the contract promises. COVERAGE: examined 1 adjacent plane pair(s) from 2 conductor(s) on the nonuniform lane (a sheet's normal plane, a volume's two faces per axis; coplanar sheet rims are not paired); physical stack computed from Box entries only — 0 non-Box dielectric entr(y/ies) ignored (said so, per #703); 0 pair(s) skipped (conductor cell between). STALE IF: re-summing the printed column disagrees with these numbers, or realized_wall_planes on the named entries does not return the printed planes.
